# qualys_vm_findings (Data Source)

Look up individual Qualys VM vulnerability findings: one affected host, one
QID, one detection instance — never aggregated by host or by QID. Where
Qualys reports the same QID on two ports of the same host as distinct
detections, this data source returns two findings. Read-only: it cannot
create, modify, suppress, acknowledge, purge or otherwise change a finding.

This is the VM counterpart to `qualys_was_findings`. It is a separate data
model from `qualys_host_detections`, which stays a per-host summary (last
scan time, tracking method, DNS/NetBIOS names) — this data source does not
alter or subsume that one; use `qualys_host_detections` for host inventory
and this one for individual vulnerability findings.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "qualys_vm_findings" "customer" {
  status = [
    "New",
    "Active",
    "Re-Opened",
  ]
}

output "vm_findings" {
  value     = data.qualys_vm_findings.customer.findings
  sensitive = true
}
```

Filtering by asset group (resolved to that group's member IPs — see
"Asset group filtering" below):

```terraform
data "qualys_vm_findings" "customer" {
  asset_group_ids = ["123456"]
}
```

Filtering by IP scope:

```terraform
data "qualys_vm_findings" "customer" {
  ips = [
    "10.20.0.0/24",
    "10.30.10.5",
  ]
}
```

Filtering by severity:

```terraform
data "qualys_vm_findings" "customer" {
  minimum_severity = 3
}
```

Filters are composable — every example above can be combined in one block.

## Finding identity

Each finding carries a stable, deterministic `finding_key`, generated as
`<host_id>:<qid>:<PROTOCOL>:<port>` (e.g. `123456:105015:TCP:443`), or
`<host_id>:<qid>` when Qualys reports no port for the detection. It is never
derived from list position or randomness, so it is identical between two
reads of unchanged Qualys data — the property a downstream diff or JSON
export depends on.

An exact duplicate finding returned across a pagination boundary is
collapsed to one record. If two decoded records share a `finding_key` but
disagree on their other fields, the first one seen is kept and a Terraform
warning diagnostic is emitted describing the conflict, rather than either
record silently winning or the two being merged.

## Ordering

`findings` is sorted by `host_id`, `qid`, `port`, `protocol` — numerically
for the numeric-looking identity fields, so host `10` sorts after host `9`
rather than before it. Two reads of unchanged data return the list in the
same order.

## Status handling

`status` is returned exactly as Qualys reports it (e.g. `New`, `Active`,
`Fixed`, `Re-Opened`) — this data source does not translate Qualys's
vulnerability lifecycle into any downstream remediation workflow's
vocabulary (such as "Open"/"In Progress"/"Accepted Risk"/"Remediated").
That mapping belongs in the consumer, not this provider.

## Asset group filtering

`asset_group_ids` is resolved by looking up each group's statically
configured IPs (via the same call `qualys_asset_group` itself uses) and
merging them into the `ips` filter. This endpoint has no confirmed
asset-group-ID query parameter of its own — see "Evidence and provenance"
below — so a group whose membership is defined purely by DNS/NetBIOS name
or by a dynamic rule, rather than a static IP list, is not fully resolved
this way. Pass `host_ids`/`ips` directly for those hosts.

## Pagination

All matching records are retrieved, following Qualys's truncation/
continuation mechanism, unless `max_results` is set. A subscription with
tens or hundreds of thousands of detections is not silently truncated to
one page.

`max_results`, when set, truncates the *returned* collection to that many
findings, taken from the front of the deterministic sort order — it does
not stop pagination early or reduce API calls. Leave it unset to return
everything.

## KnowledgeBase enrichment

Setting `enrich_with_knowledgebase = true` joins each finding's QID against
the Qualys KnowledgeBase to populate `title`, `category`, `cvss_v2_base`,
`cvss_v3_base`, `pci_flag` and `patchable`. Unique QIDs across all matching
findings are collected first and fetched in one batched request (or a small,
paginated number of them if the QID list is large enough to truncate) —
never one KnowledgeBase request per finding. A QID with no KnowledgeBase
entry (a custom or de-listed QID) simply leaves those fields empty/zero for
that finding, not an error.

The KnowledgeBase API is a separately-authorized Qualys add-on. If your
subscription lacks it, leave `enrich_with_knowledgebase` at its default
(`false`) — every other field remains fully populated.

## Empty results

No matching findings is not an error: `findings` is simply `[]`.

## Terraform state — read this before using `results`

Every field returned here is persisted in Terraform state once this data
source is read, including:

- `findings[*].results` — raw technical detail Qualys captured for the
  detection (banners, response fragments), which may contain sensitive
  information about the scanned target.
- Asset identifiers: `ip`, `dns`, `netbios`, `operating_system`.

`results` is marked `Sensitive` so `terraform plan`/`apply` output does not
print it, but **it is still stored in Terraform state in full** — Sensitive
only affects CLI output, not state file contents. Protect state accordingly
(remote state with access controls and encryption at rest), and mark any
output that re-exposes these fields `sensitive = true`, as the examples on
this page do.

## Evidence and provenance

The per-detection fields this data source exposes (`severity`, `port`,
`protocol`, `status`, the `*_datetime` fields, `results`, `times_found`,
`is_ignored`, `is_disabled`, and similar) are **Corroborated, not
Confirmed**: they reflect Qualys's long-published Host List Detection API
schema, which this session could not fetch directly (docs.qualys.com is
blocked in this sandbox) or verify against a captured tenant response.
`first_found_datetime`/`last_found_datetime` specifically are two of three
field names this provider's discovery notes already record as Confirmed for
this endpoint from the official API Quick Reference Guide (the third,
`last_scan_datetime`, is the host-level field `qualys_host_detections`
already uses) — stronger corroboration than an unsupported guess, but still
not independently verified in this session. The KnowledgeBase fields carry
the identical caveat. **Verify against a tenant, or a captured API
response, before relying on this in production.**

Two fields this session found no confident evidence for were deliberately
left out of the schema rather than guessed: a per-detection `fqdn` and a
`service` element.

`qids`, `minimum_severity`/`maximum_severity` and the six date-range filters
are applied client-side, after retrieval — this session found no confirmed
query-parameter names for QID or severity-range or date-range filtering on
this specific endpoint, and asserting an unconfirmed parameter name risks a
filter that silently does nothing if the name is wrong. `host_ids`, `ips`
and `status` are sent as real server-side query parameters — all three are
already Confirmed/used elsewhere in this provider against this same
endpoint.

## Schema

### Optional

- **host_ids** (Set of String) Restrict to these host IDs.
- **ips** (Set of String) Restrict to these IPs, hyphenated ranges or CIDR blocks.
- **asset_group_ids** (Set of String) Restrict to hosts in these asset groups. See "Asset group filtering" above.
- **qids** (Set of String) Restrict to these QIDs. Applied client-side.
- **status** (Set of String) Restrict to these Qualys detection statuses, e.g. `New`, `Active`, `Fixed`, `Re-Opened`.
- **minimum_severity** / **maximum_severity** (Number) Restrict to this severity range (1-5). Validated at plan time.
- **first_found_after** / **first_found_before** (String) RFC3339. Applied client-side.
- **last_found_after** / **last_found_before** (String) RFC3339. Applied client-side.
- **last_test_after** / **last_test_before** (String) RFC3339. Applied client-side.
- **enrich_with_knowledgebase** (Boolean) Join KnowledgeBase metadata. Defaults to `false`. See "KnowledgeBase enrichment" above.
- **max_results** (Number) Truncate the returned collection to this many findings. Every matching record is still retrieved first.

### Read-Only

- **id** (String) The ID of this data source (a digest of the matching findings' keys).
- **findings** (List of Object) Matching findings, ordered by `host_id`, `qid`, `port`, `protocol`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--findings))

<a id="nestedatt--findings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `findings`

Read-Only:

- **finding_key** (String) Stable identity — see "Finding identity" above.
- **host_id** / **ip** / **dns** / **netbios** / **operating_system** / **tracking_method** (String)
- **qid** (String)
- **port** (Number)
- **protocol** (String)
- **severity** (Number)
- **status** (String)
- **type** (String) `Confirmed` or `Potential`.
- **ssl** (Boolean)
- **results** (String, Sensitive) See "Terraform state" above.
- **first_found_datetime** / **last_found_datetime** / **last_test_datetime** / **last_update_datetime** / **last_fixed_datetime** (String)
- **times_found** (Number)
- **is_ignored** / **is_disabled** (Boolean)
- **title** / **category** (String) Populated only when `enrich_with_knowledgebase = true`.
- **cvss_v2_base** / **cvss_v3_base** (Number) Populated only when `enrich_with_knowledgebase = true`.
- **pci_flag** / **patchable** (Boolean) Populated only when `enrich_with_knowledgebase = true`.
